questions.statement: According to the first paragraph, what is the primary business advantage of the "fast fashion" model?
questions.context:
**The Fast Fashion Dilemma**
Fast fashion—the rapid production of inexpensive, trendy clothing—has revolutionized the retail industry. Brands like Zara, H&M, and Shein can design, produce, and distribute a garment globally in under three weeks. This model offers consumers affordable ways to participate in passing trends, democratizing style that was once exclusive to high-end runways.

However, the hidden costs of this convenience are devastating. The textile industry is currently the second-largest polluter of clean water globally. To keep prices abnormally low, manufacturing is outsourced to developing nations where labor laws are lax, leading to sweatshop conditions and poverty wages for garment workers, overwhelmingly women.

Furthermore, the environmental footprint is massive. Fast fashion garments are often made of synthetic, petroleum-based fabrics like polyester, which shed microplastics into the ocean with every wash. Because the clothes are cheaply made and quickly go out of style, consumers treat them as disposable. As a result, millions of tons of textiles end up in landfills or are incinerated each year.

The emerging movement of "sustainable fashion" seeks to combat this. It emphasizes buying fewer, higher-quality items, thrifting, and supporting brands that guarantee ethical labor practices and use organic or recycled materials. Yet, the question remains: can sustainable fashion scale up enough to become the norm, or will the addictive allure of a five-dollar t-shirt continue to dictate the market?

options.text: It uses only high-end, expensive runway materials.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says it produces "inexpensive" clothing.

options.text: It significantly accelerates the journey of clothing from the design phase to global distribution.
options.feedback: Correct. The text states they can "design, produce, and distribute a garment globally in under three weeks."

options.text: It relies exclusively on organic and recycled materials.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the goal of sustainable fashion, not fast fashion.

options.text: It guarantees high wages for women in developing nations.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text explicitly mentions "poverty wages".

questions.explanation:
This tests scanning for specific information. The student must link "rapid production" and "under three weeks" to the concept of accelerating the journey.

options.text: Governments will tax carbon emissions in the future to stop the anomalies.

The term is not about growth by itself.

questions.explanation:
Equity refers to fairness that accounts for unequal starting conditions.

---

questions.statement: Why does the author mention local data in the passage?
questions.context: A local report on air quality compared pollution levels near schools before and after traffic restrictions. The data showed lower emissions during school hours, which supporters used to defend the measure.

options.text: To replace all international evidence with opinion
options.feedback: The author uses data as support, not as an excuse to reject evidence.

options.text: To make the argument more concrete and verifiable for readers
options.feedback: Correct. Local data grounds the claim in observable evidence.

options.text: To show that statistics are never useful
options.feedback: That contradicts the role of the data in the passage.
The text uses data precisely to discuss policy.

questions.explanation:
Local evidence makes the argument more specific, relevant, and testable.

---

questions.statement: Choose the most accurate sentence.

options.text: The report recommends reducing emissions immediately.
options.feedback: Correct. The sentence is grammatical and uses appropriate formal register.

options.text: The report recommend reducing emissions immediately.
options.feedback: The verb does not agree with the singular subject.

options.text: The report recommending reduce emissions immediately.
options.feedback: The structure is incomplete.

options.text: The report has recommend reducing emissions immediately.
options.feedback: The auxiliary and participle are incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Formal written English requires correct agreement and verb structure.

---

questions.statement: Which statement is best supported by the set of passages?

options.text: Local action matters only when national governments fail.
options.feedback: The passages do not limit local action in that way.

options.text: Public participation is more effective when information is clear and evidence-based.
options.feedback: Correct. That idea connects the recurring emphasis on informed action.

options.text: Environmental issues can be solved without cooperation.
options.feedback: This contradicts the idea of shared responsibility.

options.text: Online communication always guarantees community engagement.
options.feedback: One passage explicitly questions that assumption.

questions.explanation:
The strongest answer captures the shared logic across the passages.

---

questions.statement: Which sentence has the most appropriate register for a formal campaign email?

options.text: Hey everyone, just fix it now.
options.feedback: The tone is too abrupt and informal.

options.text: We kindly invite residents to review the proposal and share feedback by Friday.
options.feedback: Correct. It is polite, precise, and appropriate for a formal message.

options.text: You all better answer this soon.
options.feedback: The wording is too aggressive.
The language is vague and informal.

questions.explanation:
Register questions test whether language fits the situation and audience.

---

questions.statement: Choose the option that best completes the paragraph: "The project began as a school initiative. ______, local businesses later joined and funded the expansion."

options.feedback: Correct. The second clause presents a consequence of the first stage.
That would suggest replacement, not development.
The second clause is not just an example.
The relation is not parallel.

questions.explanation:
The connector must show causal progression from one stage to the next.

---

questions.statement: What assumption does the author of the second passage seem to reject?

options.text: People are able to verify information carefully.
options.feedback: The passage does not reject that possibility outright.

options.text: Popularity online is the same as reliability.
options.feedback: Correct. The warning about misinformation challenges that assumption.

options.text: Citizens can learn media literacy skills.
options.feedback: That would support, not contradict, the passage.

options.text: Digital tools can help public communication.
options.feedback: The passage criticizes misuse, not all digital tools.

questions.explanation:
The text questions the idea that visibility or repetition guarantees truth.

---

questions.statement: Which conclusion best integrates the three passages?

options.text: Communities improve public life only through expert intervention.
options.feedback: The passages emphasize shared responsibility, not only expert action.

options.text: Sustainable change depends on informed participation, trustworthy communication, and local cooperation.
options.feedback: Correct. It combines the central ideas without exaggeration.

options.text: Technology should replace all face-to-face civic spaces.
options.feedback: The texts do not support that replacement.

options.text: Environmental action matters more than any social factor.
options.feedback: The passages link environmental and social dimensions.

questions.explanation:
A strong synthesis preserves the main contribution of each passage.

---

questions.statement: In policy discussions, the adjective "inclusive" most nearly means

options.feedback: That is the opposite of inclusive.

options.text: open to different people and perspectives
options.feedback: Correct. Inclusive policies seek broad participation and access.
That meaning is unrelated.
That does not match the term.

questions.explanation:
The meaning must fit civic and social participation contexts.

---

questions.statement: Choose the best final sentence for an argumentative paragraph about local climate action.

options.feedback: The sentence is too vague to close an argument.

options.text: For these reasons, coordinated local measures can produce measurable environmental and social benefits.
options.feedback: Correct. It closes the argument with a precise conclusion.
The wording is too uncertain and informal.

options.text: And that is why weather exists.
options.feedback: This does not conclude the argument logically.

questions.explanation:
A strong concluding sentence restates the claim with precision and purpose.

---

questions.statement: Which evaluation of the passages is the most rigorous?

options.text: They are persuasive because they use emotional words only.
options.feedback: A rigorous evaluation considers evidence and reasoning, not only tone.

options.text: They are persuasive to the extent that claims are supported by examples, data, and clear causal links.
options.feedback: Correct. This criterion evaluates the quality of the argument.

options.text: They are correct because they agree with each other.
options.feedback: Agreement alone does not prove validity.

options.text: They are weak because they discuss social problems.
options.feedback: The topic does not determine argument quality.

questions.explanation:
Critical reading evaluates how claims are justified, not just whether they agree.

---

questions.statement: What criterion best improves a final evaluation of a public-information text?

options.text: Checking only whether the topic is popular.
options.feedback: Popularity does not measure quality.

options.text: Reviewing claims, evidence, and causal links together.
options.feedback: Correct. A sound evaluation examines how the text justifies its message.

options.text: Accepting the text if it sounds technical.
options.feedback: Technical language alone is not enough.
Audience matters in public communication.

questions.explanation:
A rigorous evaluation combines content, support, and communicative purpose.

---

questions.statement: Choose the best transition for a conclusion: "The proposal reduces waste and improves participation. ______, it deserves serious consideration."

options.feedback: Correct. The connector links the reasons to the conclusion.
That marker indicates simultaneity, not conclusion.
The sentence is not contrastive.
The second clause is not an example.

questions.explanation:
The transition must signal that the conclusion follows from the previous reasons.

---

questions.statement: Ana _______ en una empresa de tecnología en Bogotá. Ella _________ sus tareas a las 8 de la mañana.
questions.context: Vida cotidiana en Bogotá

options.feedback: "Ana" es third person singular, entonces se añade -s al verbo en afirmativo
"trabajo" es primera persona singular, no concuerda con "Ana"

questions.explanation:
En presente simple, los verbos en tercera persona singular (he/she/it) añaden -s o -es. Como "Ana" es tercera persona singular, "trabaja" es la forma correcta. El error común es confundir con la primera persona o con formas incorrectas sin -s.

---
questions.icfes_type: Identificar el uso del presente simple en situaciones cotidianas

questions.statement: Los estudiantes no _______ la tarea en clase. Ellos la _______ en casa.
questions.context: Rutina diaria de un estudiante colombiano

options.feedback: Sujeto plural "Los estudiantes" requiere la forma base del verbo en negativo y la forma plural en afirmativo

questions.explanation:
Con sujeto plural (they), el presente simple no lleva -s. En negativo se usa "do not" (don't) + verbo base. El error común es añadir -s incorrectamente a verbos con sujetos plurales.

---
questions.icfes_type: Reconocer la forma negativa del presente simple

questions.statement: ¿_______ tú _________ español todos los días?
questions.context: Entrevista laboral en Medellín

options.feedback: Para formar preguntas en presente simple con "you", se invierte el orden: ¿Do you speak...? o simplemente "¿Hablas...?"

questions.explanation:
Para preguntas en presente simple con segunda persona (you), se usa "do" como auxiliar: "Do you speak...?" En español, el orden invertido indica pregunta. El error común es usar "makes" o "does" incorrectamente.

---
questions.icfes_type: Comprender el uso de auxiliares en preguntas de presente simple

questions.statement: ¿_______ su madre _________ en Cali?
questions.context: Investigación escolar sobre familias colombianas

options.feedback: Con third person singular (she), el verbo en pregunta puede ir al inicio sin auxiliar en español, o usar "Does she work...?" en inglés

questions.explanation:
En preguntas con third person singular (she), en inglés se usa "does" como auxiliar. En español, el signos de interrogación indica la pregunta. El error común es no reconocer que "hace" no es auxiliar correcto aquí.

---
questions.icfes_type: Identificar el uso de "does" con third person singular en preguntas

questions.statement: Mi hermano _________ como ingeniero de sistemas y siempre _______ nuevos proyectos.
questions.context: Perfil profesional en redes sociales

options.feedback: "Mi hermano" es third person singular, requiere -s en el verbo: "works" y "initiates"

questions.explanation:
Tercera persona singular (he/she/it) requiere verbos con -s o -es. El error común es omitir la -s con sujeto singular o añadirla con sujeto plural. La concordancia sujeto-verbo es fundamental.

---
questions.icfes_type: Aplicar las reglas de tercera persona singular en contextos reales

questions.statement: Yo siempre _______ inglés por la mañana antes de _______ a clase.
questions.context: Entrevista sobre hábitos de estudio en Cartagena

options.feedback: "Yo" es primera persona, usa la forma base del verbo sin -s. Los adverbios de frecuencia van con presente simple

questions.explanation:
Con primera persona (I) y segunda persona (you), el verbo no lleva -s. Los adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, often) se colocan antes del verbo principal. El error común es confundir personas y añadir -s incorrectamente.

---
questions.icfes_type: Usar correctamente el presente simple con adverbios de frecuencia

questions.statement: _______ el profesor de inglés _______ la tarea todos los días?
questions.context: Encuesta sobre transporte público en Barranquilla

options.feedback: Con third person singular (the teacher = he/she), en inglés se usaría "Does the English teacher review...?"

questions.explanation:
En preguntas con third person singular en inglés, se usa "does" como auxiliar seguido de la forma base del verbo. En español, el signo de interrogación indica pregunta. El error común es usar "makes" en lugar de un verbo específico.

---
questions.icfes_type: Diferenciar entre preguntas con "do" y "does" para differentes sujetos

questions.statement: Sofía no _______ la alarma por las mañanas porque ella siempre _______ temprano.
questions.context: Comparación de estilos de vida entre jóvenes en Pereira

options.feedback: "Sofía" es third person singular, por lo tanto el verbo en negativo no lleva -s después de "does not"

questions.explanation:
En negativo con third person singular: "She does not (doesn't) wake up early". El verbo mantiene la forma base. El error común es confundir la forma del verbo con la del afirmativo.

---
questions.icfes_type: Construir oraciones negativas en presente simple con diferentes sujetos

questions.statement: Ellos _______ emprendedores exitosos. Su negocio _______ en el centro de la ciudad.
questions.context: Descripción de un emprendimiento en Bucaramanga

options.feedback: El verbo "to be" (ser/estar) tiene formas especiales: am, is, are. Para "ellos" se usa "son/son"

questions.explanation:
El verbo "to be" es excepcional: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are. Para "ellos" (they) se usa "are" en inglés, equivalente a "son" en español. El error común es tratar "to be" como verbo regular.

---
questions.icfes_type: Identificar el verbo "to be" como excepción en presente simple

questions.statement: Los lunes, mi hermana _______ clases de música _______ la tarde.
questions.context: Horario semanal de una estudiante en Armenia

options.feedback: "Por la tarde" indica tiempo generalize, mientras "en la tarde" indica momento específico. "Por" se usa con partes del día en presente simple

questions.explanation:
"Por la mañana/tarde/noche" se usa para indicar tiempo generalize en acciones habituales. El error común es usar "en" indistintamente sin considerar el matiz de generalidad vs. especificidad.

---
questions.icfes_type: Usar expresiones de tiempo con presente simple

questions.statement: Los profesores _______ mucho. Nosotros _______ mucho también.
questions.context: Corrección de oraciones en un examen de inglés en Cali

options.feedback: "Los profesores" es plural (they), entonces el verbo no lleva -s. "Nosotros" es first person plural, usa "estudiamos"

questions.explanation:
La concordancia sujeto-verbo en presente simple requiere: plural subjects = verbo sin -s. El error común es añadir -s a verbos con sujetos plurales o viceversa.

---
questions.icfes_type: Analizar errores comunes en la formación del presente simple en learner English

questions.statement: Mi abuela siempre _______ arepas para el desayuno. Ella _______ ingredientas frescos.
questions.context: Actividad de editing en un curso de inglés en Neiva

options.feedback: "Mi abuela" (she) requiere third person singular: "makes" (-s) y "uses" (-s)

questions.explanation:
Con third person singular, ambos verbos deben llevar -s: makes/uses. El error común es la inconsistencia: usar -s en un verbo pero no en otro cuando ambos corresponden al mismo sujeto.

---
questions.icfes_type: Evaluar la corrección de oraciones en presente simple

questions.statement: ¿____ María _______ el vuelo a Bogotá mañana?
questions.context: Role-play en una agencia de viajes en Santa Marta

options.feedback: La pregunta "Does Maria reserve the flight...?" en español se transforma usando signos de interrogación sin cambiar el orden del verbo

questions.explanation:
Para preguntas con third person singular en inglés se usa "does" como auxiliar. En español, el orden puede mantenerse si los signos de interrogación indican claramente la pregunta. El error común es usar verbos genéricos como "makes" en lugar de verbos específicos.

---
questions.icfes_type: Identificar y corregir errores en el uso de auxiliares en preguntas

questions.statement: La librería _______ a las 9 de la mañana y _______ hasta las 7 de la tarde. El dueño _______ libros de historia.
questions.context: Descripción de una librería en Villa de Leyva

options.feedback: Todos los sujetos son third person singular: la librería, (él), por lo tanto verbos en -s

questions.explanation:
Tercera persona singular (she/it) requiere verbos con -s. La librería = it, el dueño = he. El error común es mezclar formas plurales con singulares o viceversa.

---
questions.icfes_type: Producir texto coherente aplicando presente simple en narraciones breves

questions.statement: Los turistas _______ el café de la región. Ellas siempre _______ el clima cálido.
questions.context: Blog de viajes sobreSalento, Quindío

options.feedback: "Los turistas" (they) y "ellas" (they) son sujetos plurales que requieren verbos sin -s

questions.explanation:
Los sujetos plurales (they) requieren la forma base del verbo sin -s. "Aman" y "disfrutan" son las formas correctas. El error común es usar third person singular forms con sujetos plurales.

---
questions.icfes_type: Distinguir entre formas verbales correctas e incorrectas en contexto

questions.statement: La gente _______ al lago porque _______ cuidar el medio ambiente.
questions.context: Charla sobre contaminación en Laguna de Tota

options.feedback: "La gente" es singular en español pero se trata como plural (they) en inglés. En español se mantiene singular: "respeta" y "decide"

questions.explanation:
"La gente" en español es singular, por lo tanto "respeta" y "decide" son correctos. En inglés, "people" es plural y requiere "respect" y "decide" (sin -s). El error común es pensar que "gente" funciona como "people" en inglés directamente.

---
questions.icfes_type: Seleccionar la mejor opción gramatical en contexto comunicativo

questions.statement: Carlos _______ escultura porque él _______ el arte prehispánico. Su trabajo _______ en museos internacionales.
questions.context: Perfil de un artista de San Agustín, Huila

options.feedback: "Carlos" (he) requiere verbos en -s en inglés. En español, "estudia", "ama" y "se exhibe" concuerdan con el sujeto singular

questions.explanation:
Tercera persona singular (he/she/it) en inglés requiere -s en verbos. En español, tercera persona singular no tiene marca visible en infinitivos. El error común es omitir -s en inglés o añadirlo incorrectamente.

---
questions.icfes_type: Construir párrafos coherentes usando presente simple con diferentes estructuras

questions.statement: Mis padres no _______ redes sociales. Mi madre _______ correos electrónicos todos los días.
questions.context: Comparación de hábitos tecnológicos entre generaciones en Manizales

options.feedback: "Mis padres" es plural: "usan" sin -s. "Mi madre" es singular: "envía" con -s

questions.explanation:
Sujetos plurales y singulares en la misma oración requieren formas verbales diferentes. "Usan" para plural (parents), "envía" para singular (mother). El error común es no mantener la consistencia o confundir los sujetos.

---
questions.icfes_type: Analizar estructuras gramaticales complejas con múltiples sujeto

questions.statement: El café de Nariño _______ en las montañas. Los agricultores _______ el café manualmente.
questions.context: Artículo sobre producción de café en Nariño

options.feedback: "El café" (it) es third person singular: "is cultivated" (-s). "Los agricultores" (they) son plural: "harvest" (sin -s)

questions.explanation:
La voz pasiva en presente simple con third person singular usa "is/are + past participle". Sujetos plurales usan "are". El error común es no concordar el verbo auxiliar con el sujeto.

---
questions.icfes_type: Evaluar la precisión gramatical en textos descriptivos

questions.statement: Los jóvenes colombianos _______ empresas innovadoras porque _______ cambiar el mundo. Ella _______ como líder de su comunidad.
questions.context: Discusión sobre emprendimiento juvenil en Colombia

options.feedback: "Los jóvenes" (they) plural: "crean", "desean". "Ella" (she) singular: "destaca" con -s en inglés

questions.explanation:
Crear texto con sujetos mixtos requiere cambiar entre formas plurales y singulares. La coherencia gramatical es esencial para la comunicación clara. El error común es la inconsistencia en el uso de personas gramaticales dentro del mismo texto.

---

**End of Bundle**
questions.icfes_type: Crear texto original aplicando correctamente las reglas del presente simple

questions.statement:
Read the following advertisement from a travel magazine:

"Discover the magic of Cartagena! Walk through the colorful streets of the old city, enjoy the crystal-clear waters of the Caribbean, and taste the delicious flavors of Colombian cuisine. Book your dream vacation today at www.cartagenaparadise.co"

What is the main purpose of this text?
questions.context: Colombian tourism advertisement

options.text: To describe the historical importance of Cartagena's fort

options.feedback: The text uses persuasive language like "dream vacation" and "magic" to encourage people to visit Cartagena

options.text: To explain how to cook traditional Colombian food
To compare Cartagena with other Caribbean destinations
options.feedback: The text does not make any comparison with other destinations

questions.explanation:
This question tests the student's ability to identify the main purpose of a text. The advertisement clearly aims to persuade readers to visit Cartagena, using marketing language and listing attractions. The distractors represent common errors: confusing promotional text with informative historical content (A), misidentifying the topic of "Colombian cuisine" as the main focus (C), and assuming comparative structure when none exists (D).

---

questions.statement:
Look at this excerpt from the TransMilenio schedule at a station in Bogotá:

"Portal Norte - Station: Estadio
First bus: 5:00 AM
Last bus: 11:00 PM
Frequency: Every 4 minutes during peak hours
Alimentador connections available"

What time does the last Alimentador bus leave Estadio station?
questions.context: Public transportation schedule

options.text: The text does not specify this information
options.feedback: The schedule only mentions that Alimentador connections are "available" but does not specify their operating hours or departure times

questions.explanation:
This question assesses the student's ability to identify information that is NOT present in the text. Students often assume they can infer details that aren't explicitly stated. Option C is a common distractor because they might confuse the "Last bus" information (11:00 PM) with the Alimentador schedule. Option B is a distractor testing confusion between frequency and departure times.

---

questions.statement:
Read the email from the Universidad de los Andes admissions office:

"Dear prospective student,
Thank you for your interest in our Engineering program. After reviewing your application, we have decided to move forward with candidates whose profiles more closely match our current institutional needs. We encourage you to apply again next semester and wish you the best in your academic journey."

What can be inferred about the applicant's status?
questions.context: Email from university

options.text: They have been accepted into the Engineering program
Their application was not selected for this period
options.feedback: The phrase "move forward with candidates" and the encouragement to reapply indicates the applicant was not selected

options.text: They need to submit additional documents
They have been waitlisted for the program
options.feedback: The email does not mention a waitlist; it suggests reapplying, implying rejection

questions.explanation:
This question tests inferential comprehension. Students must read between the lines to understand that "moving forward with other candidates" means rejection. The formal, polite tone is designed to soften bad news, which can confuse students who mistake politeness for acceptance. Option D is a plausible distractor because waitlisting is a real possibility students might assume.

---

questions.statement:
A Colombian environmental organization posts on Instagram:

"🌍 Our planet is dying. People keep throwing trash on the streets. If we don't change NOW, Colombia will be a huge landfill. Share this post if you care about your country!"

Based on this post, what is the author's primary intention?
questions.context: Social media post about recycling

options.text: To inform citizens about proper recycling methods
To celebrate successful environmental policies in Colombia
To persuade people to share the post and raise awareness
options.feedback: The explicit call to action "Share this post" combined with emotional language reveals the main goal is viral mobilization, not education

options.text: To recruit volunteers for beach cleanups
options.feedback: There's no mention of volunteering or specific cleanup activities

questions.explanation:
Students often confuse emotional appeals with informative intent. This question requires analyzing the rhetorical devices (dramatic language, call to action) to determine purpose. Option A is a plausible distractor because environmental topics often involve education. Option D might seem logical since environmental organizations do recruit volunteers, but the text provides no evidence for this specific claim.

---

questions.statement:
Read the following excerpt from an article about Colombian coffee:

"The Colombian coffee crisis of the 1990s forced many small farmers to **abandon** their lands and migrate to cities like Medellín and Bogotá. Without government support, they had few options but to seek new opportunities in urban areas."

The word "abandon" in this context most nearly means:
questions.context: Article about Colombian coffee industry

options.feedback: In this context, "abandon" means to leave behind, often reluctantly. The farmers left their lands due to economic crisis, not to destroy them
"Abandon" implies finality; visiting occasionally does not fit the context of migration

questions.explanation:
Context clues are essential here. The sentence explains that farmers "migrated to cities" and "sought new opportunities," indicating they left their lands permanently due to crisis. Option A confuses "abandon" with destructive intent. Option C incorrectly assumes economic transaction. Option D contradicts the permanent nature of migration described.

---
questions.icfes_type: Identificar el significado de palabras en contexto

questions.statement:
A food critic writes about a restaurant in the Zona Rosa of Bogotá:

"The restaurant 'Sabor Paisa' offers authentic Antioqueño cuisine in a cozy atmosphere. The portion sizes are generous, and prices are moderate for the neighborhood. However, service can be slow during weekend evenings, and reservations are strongly recommended."

If a student wants to celebrate a birthday at this restaurant with 10 friends on a Saturday night, what should they do according to the review?
questions.context: Restaurant review in digital magazine

options.text: Order for delivery since dine-in service is too slow
Expect to pay premium prices due to the location
Make a reservation well in advance
options.feedback: The text explicitly states "reservations are strongly recommended," especially relevant for a large group on a Saturday

options.text: Request a different day since the restaurant is closed on weekends
options.feedback: The review mentions slow service on weekends, not closure

questions.explanation:
This question tests whether students can extract actionable advice from a review. The explicit recommendation to make reservations is the key information. Option A is a logical leap that ignores the context of a celebration. Option B contradicts "moderate prices." Option D misreads "slow service" as "closure."

---
questions.icfes_type: Aplicar información del texto a nuevas situaciones

questions.statement:
A patient reads the following instructions on a prescription bottle:

"Take one tablet by mouth, twice daily with food. Do not operate heavy machinery. Avoid alcohol. If side effects occur, contact your doctor immediately."

What is the purpose of this text?
questions.context: Instructions on medication label

options.text: To advertise a new medication to doctors
To explain how to prepare the medication
To ensure the patient uses the medication safely
options.feedback: The warnings about machinery, alcohol, and side effects indicate the text's purpose is safety and proper usage

options.text: To describe the ingredients of the medication
options.feedback: No ingredients are listed; the focus is on usage instructions

questions.explanation:
Students may confuse prescription instructions with advertising (A) or preparation procedures (B). The safety warnings are the clear indicator of purpose here. Option D is a plausible error because people often assume medication labels list ingredients, but this label focuses on usage protocol.

---

questions.statement:
Read the synopsis from a Colombian streaming platform:

"In the biopic 'Colombian Star,' we follow the journey of salsa legend Celia Cruz from her humble beginnings in Havana to her rise as the 'Queen of Salsa.' The film explores her complicated relationship with her family, her struggles with the music industry, and her ultimate triumph at the Grammy Awards."

How is the information in this synopsis organized?
questions.context: Movie synopsis from entertainment guide

options.feedback: The synopsis moves from "humble beginnings" to "rise" to "ultimate triumph," following the natural timeline of Celia's life
No cause-effect relationship is presented; it's a life narrative ordered by time

questions.explanation:
This question tests text structure recognition. The key words "beginnings," "rise," and "ultimate triumph" indicate a life trajectory. Option A is a distractor because while there are challenges, no explicit problem-solution structure exists. Option C might attract students who think the film compares Celia to other artists. Option D confuses narrative arc with causal logic.

---

questions.statement:
The weather forecast for the upcoming week in Medellín shows:

Monday: Sunny, 28°C
Tuesday: Partly cloudy, 26°C
Wednesday: Thunderstorms expected, 24°C
Thursday: Heavy rain, 23°C
Friday: Clearing, 25°C

What can be inferred about outdoor plans for Wednesday?
questions.context: Weather forecast

options.text: They will be perfect due to the warm temperature
They should be postponed due to expected thunderstorms
options.feedback: "Thunderstorms expected" clearly indicates risky weather for outdoor activities

options.text: They will be cancelled because it will rain heavily
They will be better on Friday since it's the end of the week
options.feedback: While Friday looks better, the question asks about Wednesday specifically, not about comparing days

questions.explanation:
This question requires connecting weather data to practical decision-making. Students may overgeneralize "thunderstorms" as complete cancellation (C), or they might make a comparison that isn't asked (D). Option A fails to recognize that thunderstorms are dangerous regardless of temperature. The correct answer tests focused inference from Wednesday's specific forecast.

---

questions.statement:
An opinion piece in El Tiempo discusses the future of work in Colombia:

"While automation will eliminate some jobs, it will create many more. We should focus on retraining workers for the digital economy rather than resisting technological change. Our education system must adapt, or Colombia will fall behind other nations."

What is the author's main argument?
questions.context: Opinion column in newspaper

options.text: Automation is harmful to Colombian workers
Robots should replace all manual labor jobs
Education reform is necessary to prepare workers for automation

questions.statement:

Option D is incorrect because no attacks on individuals occur.

Despite these limitations, we maintain that our findings accurately represent the overall trend."

options.feedback: The comparison is a valid analytical approach; it does not weaken the study

questions.explanation:
Students must evaluate which methodological limitation most seriously compromises conclusions. While the study acknowledges multiple limitations, the 15% ground truthing coverage is the most severe because satellite imagery alone, especially with resolution limitations, cannot provide complete accuracy. Option A is a standard scientific method. Option C's seven-year period is appropriate. Option D represents sound comparative methodology.

Correct. "Widen inequalities" means make them larger.
Incorrect. The sentence does not refer to measurement.

questions.explanation:
Lexical meaning should be inferred from the phrase it appears in.

---

questions.statement: Choose the best option: "By the time we arrived, the seminar ______."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The tense does not fit the completed earlier action.
Incorrect. Present perfect is not the best match with the past reference.
Correct. Past perfect marks an action completed before another past action.
Incorrect. The structure is awkward and inaccurate here.

questions.explanation:
Past perfect helps order two actions that both happened in the past.

---

questions.statement: Select the correct option: "Neither the teachers nor the principal ______ available this morning."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The subject nearest the verb is singular.
Correct. In this structure, the verb agrees with "the principal".
Incorrect. The time marker points to the past, not the present.
Incorrect. The sentence requires a simpler past form.

questions.explanation:
With `neither...nor`, verb agreement often follows the subject closest to the verb.

---

questions.statement: Which statement best summarizes the debate?
questions.context:
Read the short text:
"Several cities are redesigning streets to make them safer for cyclists and pedestrians. Supporters argue that these changes reduce pollution and traffic injuries, while critics claim they may slow down car travel in the short term."

options.text: Everyone agrees that car travel should be banned.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text does not state that.

options.text: The redesign has no effect on pollution or safety.
options.feedback: Incorrect. That contradicts the supporters' argument.

options.text: The changes may improve safety and the environment, but some people worry about traffic flow.
options.feedback: Correct. It includes both perspectives.

options.text: Cyclists reject street redesign in every city.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not supported by the passage.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer captures the contrast between the two sides of the argument.

---

questions.statement: Why does the author include the critics' perspective?

options.text: To prove that redesign plans always fail.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author does not conclude that.

options.text: To change the topic from safety to tourism.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text stays on urban mobility.

options.text: To show that the policy has trade-offs and not only benefits.
options.feedback: Correct. The text presents a balanced debate.

options.text: To argue that pollution is irrelevant in cities.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This idea is absent from the passage.

questions.explanation:
Writers often include contrasting voices to show complexity and balance.

---

questions.statement: Choose the most accurate sentence.

options.text: She suggested to go earlier to avoid traffic.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After "suggested", this pattern is incomplete here.

options.text: She suggested going earlier to avoid traffic.
options.feedback: Correct. "Suggest" is naturally followed by a gerund in this structure.

options.text: She suggested that go earlier to avoid traffic.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The clause structure is incorrect.

options.text: She suggested went earlier to avoid traffic.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The verb form is not grammatical.

questions.explanation:
Verb patterns matter: `suggest` is commonly followed by `-ing` or a full clause.

---

questions.statement:
Choose the best completion:
"The report was so ______ that even non-specialists could understand the results."

options.feedback: Incorrect. That means difficult to understand, which contradicts the sentence.
Correct. A clear report can be understood by non-specialists.
Incorrect. That refers to time, not comprehension.
Incorrect. Cost does not fit the meaning needed.

questions.explanation:
The sentence requires an adjective that matches the idea of easy understanding.

---

questions.statement: What assumption do both sides share?
questions.context:
Read the short text:
"Some schools have replaced traditional exams with projects and portfolios. Advocates say this approach measures deeper learning and creativity. Critics, however, argue that scoring can become less consistent unless teachers use clear criteria."

options.text: Creativity should be removed from education.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Neither side argues that.

options.text: Assessment methods influence how student learning is judged.
options.feedback: Correct. Both sides discuss how evaluation works.

options.text: Portfolios are easier to score than any exam.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Critics suggest the opposite may happen.
Incorrect. This is not stated by both sides.

questions.explanation:
Advanced reading may ask for common ground, not just explicit disagreement.

---

questions.statement: Choose the sentence with the best formal register for an academic email.

options.text: Hey teacher, I need the file ASAP.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The register is too informal.

options.text: Send me the document when you can.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is understandable but not the most formal option.

options.text: Could you please share the document at your earliest convenience?
options.feedback: Correct. The wording is polite and suitably formal.

options.text: I want the document right now, thanks.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The tone is too direct and inappropriate.

questions.explanation:
Pragmatic competence includes choosing language that fits context and relationship.

---

questions.statement: Which conclusion is most justified by the text?
questions.context:
Read the short text:
"A city wants to introduce electric buses. Officials argue that the change will reduce emissions and improve public health. Some residents support the plan, but others worry about the initial investment and the reliability of charging infrastructure."

options.text: The city should reject the proposal because public transport never improves health.
options.feedback: Incorrect. That contradicts the officials' argument.

options.text: The plan has only economic benefits and no environmental value.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text explicitly mentions emissions and health.

options.text: The proposal offers long-term environmental advantages, but its implementation depends on solving practical and financial concerns.
options.feedback: Correct. It integrates both support and concern.

options.text: Residents oppose every form of technological change in public transport.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says some residents support the plan.

questions.explanation:
The strongest conclusion uses all the relevant evidence without exaggeration.

---

questions.statement:
Which sentence best completes the paragraph?
"Students often believe that learning a language means memorizing long word lists. ______, real progress usually depends on using words in meaningful contexts."

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would introduce an illustration, not a contrast.
Incorrect. The relation is contrastive, not parallel.
Correct. It contrasts a common belief with the author's view.
Incorrect. The second sentence is not a result of the first; it challenges it.

questions.explanation: Discourse markers organize meaning. Here the paragraph needs a contrastive connector.

questions.statement: As cities become more crowded, architects are looking ____ new ways to integrate nature into urban environments.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Look at" means to direct one's eyes, but the context requires searching for a solution.
Correct. "Look for" is the phrasal verb used for searching or seeking something.
Incorrect. "Look after" means to take care of someone or something.
Incorrect. "Look up" means to search for information in a reference or to admire someone.

questions.explanation:
Phrasal verbs (Look). Identifying the correct preposition to convey the meaning of searching for solutions.

---

questions.statement: Vertical forests are buildings ____ with hundreds of trees and shrubs.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs to be a past participle used as an adjective or part of a passive structure.
Correct. A past participle used to describe the state of the buildings.
Incorrect. This would imply the buildings are actively performing the action of covering something else.
Incorrect. This is a third-person singular verb and doesn't fit the sentence structure.

questions.explanation:
Participles as adjectives. Recognizing the passive description of the buildings.

---

questions.statement: This innovation ____ to reduce carbon dioxide levels and provide natural cooling.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The verb must be in the passive voice or present perfect to fit the context.
Correct. Passive voice (present simple) used to describe the purpose of the innovation.
Incorrect. Past continuous doesn't fit a general statement about an innovation's purpose.
Incorrect. This would imply the innovation itself performed the action of designing something.

questions.explanation:
Passive Voice. Understanding that the innovation is the recipient of the design action.

---

questions.statement: Experts believe that if more cities ____ these designs, urban temperatures would decrease significantly.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The second conditional requires the past simple in the 'if' clause.
Correct. Second conditional structure: "if + past simple, would + infinitive".
Incorrect. This belongs to the first conditional.
Incorrect. Doesn't fit the hypothetical "would" in the main clause.

questions.explanation:
Conditionals (Second Conditional). Matching the hypothetical condition with the appropriate verb tense.

---

questions.statement: However, maintaining these living walls is more expensive ____ traditional landscaping.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Used in "as...as" structures for equality, not for comparisons of superiority.
Incorrect. "That" is not used for introducing the second part of a comparative adjective.
Correct. "Than" is used to introduce the second element in a comparison.
Incorrect. While used with "different from", it is not used with comparative adjectives like "more expensive".

questions.explanation:
Comparatives. Recognizing the standard marker for comparative structures in English.

---

questions.statement: What is the primary goal of the circular economy according to the text?
questions.context: The linear "take-make-waste" model has dominated global production for decades, leading to unprecedented resource depletion. In contrast, the circular economy aims to decouple economic growth from resource consumption. By designing products that are durable, repairable, and recyclable, businesses can minimize their environmental footprint.

options.text: To increase the speed of global production.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text suggests the current model is problematic, not that we should speed it up.

options.text: To separate economic growth from the use of natural resources.
options.feedback: Correct. The text explicitly mentions "decouple economic growth from resource consumption."

options.text: To eliminate all costs associated with manufacturing.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text mentions that transition costs can be high, not that they are eliminated.

options.text: To encourage consumers to buy more products frequently.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text promotes durability and repairability, which reduces frequency of purchase.

questions.explanation:
Literal comprehension and paraphrasing. Identifying the core definition provided in the passage.

---

questions.statement: The word "depletion" in the first paragraph most likely means:

options.feedback: Incorrect. The context of "waste" and "taking" suggests a negative impact on resources.
Correct. Resource depletion refers to the exhaustion or significant reduction of available resources.
Incorrect. This would contradict the description of the "take-make-waste" model.
Incorrect. The text focuses on the consumption of resources, not finding new ones.

questions.explanation:
Vocabulary in Context. Inferring the meaning of an academic term based on the surrounding negative connotations.

---

questions.statement: According to the text, what is a potential disadvantage of transitioning to a circular economy?

options.feedback: Correct. The text mentions that "transition costs can be high."
Incorrect. Brand loyalty is listed as a long-term benefit, not a disadvantage.
Incorrect. Supply chain resilience is listed as a benefit.

options.text: A lack of durable product designs.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This option does not fit the grammatical or contextual requirements of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Detail identification. Distinguishing between benefits and challenges mentioned in the text.

---

questions.statement: What does the term "greenwashing" (mentioned as a concern) refer to?

options.text: Cleaning industrial equipment with environmentally friendly soaps.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a literal and incorrect interpretation of the term.

options.text: Making false or exaggerated claims about a company's environmental efforts.
options.feedback: Correct. It refers to adopting practices on a "superficial level" without real commitment.

options.text: The process of recycling water used in large factories.
options.feedback: Incorrect. While "washing" is mentioned, the term "greenwashing" is a metaphor for deceptive marketing.

options.text: A mandatory international regulation for all manufacturing companies.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text states that greenwashing happens "without" such regulations.

questions.explanation:
Inferential meaning. Understanding a specific socio-economic term within a critical context.

---

questions.statement: What is the author's tone regarding the circular economy?

options.feedback: Incorrect. The author mentions significant long-term benefits.
Incorrect. The author acknowledges high costs and the risk of greenwashing.
Correct. The author presents the concept, the benefits, and the potential pitfalls/criticisms.
Incorrect. The use of words like "unprecedented" and "challenge" shows engagement with the topic.

questions.explanation:
Tone analysis. Evaluating the presentation of multiple perspectives to determine the author's stance.

---

questions.statement: Which of the following would be an example of a circular economy practice?

options.text: Designing a phone that is glued shut and impossible to open.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This prevents repairability, which is a circular principle.

options.text: Offering a discount to customers who buy a new model every year.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This encourages resource consumption and waste.

options.text: A clothing brand that offers free lifetime repairs for its jackets.
options.feedback: Correct. This promotes durability and extends the product's life cycle.

options.text: Moving a factory to a country with fewer environmental laws.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This does not address resource consumption or waste management.

questions.explanation:
Application of concepts. Applying the principles of circularity described in the text to a real-world scenario.

---

questions.statement: What can be inferred about the "critics" of corporate action in this context?

options.text: They believe the circular economy is an impossible dream.
options.feedback: Incorrect. They don't say it's impossible, just that it might be done superficially.

options.text: They think voluntary corporate actions are insufficient to protect the environment.
options.feedback: Correct. They argue that strict regulations are needed to prevent superficial adoption.

options.text: They are against any form of economic growth.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text doesn't suggest they oppose growth, only how it is achieved.

options.text: They work for companies that profit from the linear model.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a possible real-world assumption, but it is not supported by the text.

questions.explanation:
Inference from text. Identifying the underlying assumption of a group mentioned in the passage.

---

questions.statement: The phrase "outweigh the initial investment" suggests that:

options.text: The investment is too heavy to be carried by small companies.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a literal and incorrect interpretation of "outweigh".

options.text: The long-term gains are more significant than the starting costs.
options.feedback: Correct. "Outweigh" means to be more important or valuable than something else.

options.text: Companies should avoid investing in circular practices.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The phrase suggests the opposite—that the investment is worth it.

options.text: Initial costs are increasing every year.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The phrase compares costs to benefits, not to time.

questions.explanation:
Metaphorical/Academic language. Understanding how comparative verbs function in an economic argument.

---

questions.statement: The global shift toward renewable energy sources ____ by the urgent need to mitigate climate change.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs the passive voice because the shift is being caused by the "need".
Correct. Present continuous passive voice used to describe an ongoing process.
Incorrect. This would imply the "shift" is the one doing the driving.
Incorrect. Past simple suggests the shift is over, while it is still happening.

questions.explanation:
Advanced Tense Control. Recognizing the need for the passive voice in a formal description of a global trend.

---

questions.statement: ____ solar and wind power are becoming cheaper, integrating them into existing power grids remains a technical challenge.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Despite" must be followed by a noun or gerund, not a full clause with a verb.
Correct. Used to introduce a concessive clause ("Although + subject + verb").
Incorrect. Usually starts a new sentence or is used after a semi-colon, not to introduce a dependent clause.
Incorrect. This indicates a result, but the sentence structure shows a contrast.

questions.explanation:
Connectors (Concession). Distinguishing between different ways to express contrast based on the grammatical structure of the sentence.

---

questions.statement: This is ____ because these sources are intermittent, meaning they do not produce energy constantly.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This means "rarely", which contradicts the explanation that intermittency is a major, common reason for the technical challenge.
Correct. Used to emphasize the main reason for something in a formal context.
Incorrect. This means "hardly", which doesn't fit the context of explaining a major challenge.
Incorrect. This means "approximately", which doesn't fit the explanation of a cause.

questions.explanation:
Adverbs of degree/emphasis. Selecting the most appropriate word to highlight the main cause in an academic text.

---

questions.statement: Which of the following statements provides the strongest critique of the "Circular Economy" model as described?

options.text: Consumers are not interested in buying durable products because they prefer new trends.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a market observation, but doesn't necessarily critique the structural model described.

options.text: If circularity is only implemented at a local level, global resource depletion will continue unabated due to the interconnected nature of modern trade.
options.feedback: Correct. This addresses the systemic limitation of the model if it's not globally regulated.

options.text: Recycling is a difficult process that requires a lot of energy and specialized machines.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a technical challenge, but it is already factored into the concept of circularity.

options.text: Most companies are too small to afford the transition costs mentioned in the article.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a financial barrier, but not a critique of the model's validity or effectiveness.

questions.explanation:
Critical thinking and synthesis. Identifying a high-level systemic critique that goes beyond the immediate challenges mentioned in the text.

---

questions.statement: The author most likely includes the mention of "greenwashing" to:

options.text: Discourage companies from ever trying to be environmentally friendly.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author supports circularity but warns about its misuse.

options.text: Show that international regulations are unnecessary and annoying for businesses.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The mention suggests that regulations might be necessary to prevent this issue.

options.text: Temper the enthusiasm for the circular economy with a warning about potential corporate deception.
options.feedback: Correct. It provides a realistic counterpoint to the benefits described earlier.

options.text: Explain why linear models are still better for the global economy.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author clearly describes the linear model as problematic.

questions.explanation:
Identifying rhetorical purpose. Understanding why an author introduces a negative concept in a generally positive or neutral explanation.

---

questions.statement: Based on the logic of the entire discussion, which of these headlines would the author most likely agree with?

options.text: "The End of Economic Growth: Why We Must Stop Producing Now."
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author talks about "decoupling" growth, not stopping it.

options.text: "Beyond the Hype: The Structural Requirements for a Truly Circular Future."
options.feedback: Correct. Reflects the need for more than just superficial changes (addressing greenwashing and regulation).

options.text: "Linear Success: How the Traditional Model Saved the Industrial World."
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author highlights the negative consequences of the linear model.

options.text: "The Cost of Green: Why Environmentalism is Only for the Wealthy."
options.feedback: Incorrect. While costs are mentioned, the focus is on business models and global impact, not social class.

questions.explanation:
Synthesizing the overall message. Selecting a title that captures both the core concept and the critical nuances of the text.

---

questions.statement: Which sentence best maintains the academic register and captures the core tension of the text?

options.text: It's great that companies want to help the Earth, but some are just lying to get more money.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Too informal ("It's great", "lying", "get more money").

options.text: Circularity is a cool way to fix the planet, even if it's super expensive at first.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Too informal ("cool", "fix the planet", "super expensive").

options.text: While the circular model offers a viable path toward sustainability, its efficacy is contingent upon rigorous regulatory oversight to prevent disingenuous corporate adoption.
options.feedback: Correct. Uses academic vocabulary ("efficacy", "contingent upon", "rigorous", "disingenuous") and captures the main argument.

options.text: Companies should stop wasting stuff and start recycling everything because it's the right thing to do.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Overly simplistic and moralizing rather than analytical.

questions.explanation: Register and precision. Identifying the most formal and accurate summary of a complex argument.

questions.statement: In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has advanced at ____ unprecedented pace.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Unprecedented" begins with a vowel sound, requiring "an".
Correct. The indefinite article "an" is used before words starting with a vowel sound.
Incorrect. While possible in some contexts, "at an unprecedented pace" is the standard idiomatic expression.
Incorrect. "Some" is not used before a singular countable noun modified by an adjective in this manner.

questions.explanation:
Articles and Phonology. Recognizing the correct indefinite article based on the following vowel sound.

---

questions.statement: This process, ____ as deep learning, allows machines to recognize patterns.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the base form and doesn't fit the reduced relative clause.
Incorrect. This would imply the process itself is doing the "knowing".
Correct. A past participle used in a reduced relative clause (which is known as).
Incorrect. Past tense doesn't fit the descriptive context.

questions.explanation:
Reduced Relative Clauses. Identifying the past participle needed to describe a concept's definition.

---

questions.statement: ____, the lack of transparency in how these decisions are made has raised significant concerns.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is used for adding supporting information, not introducing a contrast.
Correct. Used to introduce a contrasting point or a problem related to the previous statement.
Incorrect. This indicates a result, but the sentence introduces a new concern.
Incorrect. This is used for comparisons of likeness.

questions.explanation:
Logical Connectors. Choosing the correct transition word to signal a shift from advancement to concern.

---

questions.statement: Experts argue that we ____ prioritize "explainability" to ensure that AI systems remain accountable.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Suggests a weak possibility rather than the strong recommendation implied.
Incorrect. Suggests uncertainty.
Correct. Expresses a strong necessity or obligation, which fits the tone of expert advice.
Incorrect. Refers to past habits, which is irrelevant to a recommendation for the future.

questions.explanation:
Modal Verbs. Determining the appropriate level of necessity in a formal recommendation.

---

questions.statement: If developers ____ more attention to ethical frameworks earlier, some current biases might have been avoided.

options.feedback: Incorrect. While "paid" is the past of "pay", the third conditional requires "had paid".
Correct. Third conditional structure for hypothetical past situations: "if + past perfect, would have + past participle".
Incorrect. This belongs to the present perfect or first conditional.
Incorrect. "Would" is not used in the "if" clause of standard conditional sentences.

questions.explanation:
Conditionals (Third Conditional). Recognizing the structure for expressing hypothetical analysis of past events.

---

questions.statement: According to the text, why can algorithms be biased?
questions.context: Many people believe that because algorithms are based on mathematics, they are inherently objective. However, AI systems are trained on datasets that often reflect human prejudices. For instance, if a hiring algorithm is trained on historical data from a company that primarily hired men in the past, the system might learn to penalize female candidates.

options.text: Because computers have their own personal opinions.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text implies they are not sentient in a "human sense."

options.text: Because they learn from data that contains human prejudices.
options.feedback: Correct. The text explains they reflect prejudices present in the training datasets.

options.text: Because mathematics is a biased and subjective science.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text implies the math itself is neutral, but the data is the problem.

options.text: Because they are programmed to ignore male candidates.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The example given is the opposite.

questions.explanation:
Cause and Effect in Reading. Identifying the source of algorithmic bias described in the passage.

---

questions.statement: In the context of the passage, the word "inherently" most likely means:

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Inherently" suggests a permanent, natural quality.

options.text: Naturally or by its very nature.
options.feedback: Correct. "Inherently objective" means that objectivity is a fundamental part of its nature.
Incorrect. The word doesn't imply hidden actions.
Incorrect. While bias is unfair, "inherently" describes how a quality exists.

questions.explanation:
Academic Vocabulary. Determining the meaning of an adverb that describes the fundamental nature of a concept.

---

questions.statement: What is the author's primary recommendation for solving algorithmic bias?

options.text: Stopping the use of all hiring algorithms.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The author doesn't suggest banning them, but improving how they are made.

options.text: Teaching computers to understand human emotions better.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not mentioned as a solution for bias in the text.

options.text: Combining technical solutions with a diverse workforce.
options.feedback: Correct. The text mentions "technical fixes" and a "diverse group of developers."

options.text: Deleting all historical data from company records.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text doesn't suggest deleting data, but being aware of its pitfalls.

questions.explanation:
Identifying Solutions. Synthesizing the final suggestion of the author regarding diverse development teams.

---

questions.statement: What does the "hiring algorithm" example demonstrate?

options.text: That men are generally more qualified than women.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the bias the algorithm might learn, not a fact the text supports.

options.text: That computers are better than humans at hiring.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The example shows a failure of the computer's objectivity.

options.text: How historical patterns can be incorrectly turned into rules.
options.feedback: Correct. It shows how past biases are codified into future "mathematical" decisions.

options.text: That companies should never use data from the past.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The point is about how the data is used, not a total rejection.

questions.explanation:
Interpreting Examples. Understanding the rhetorical purpose of a specific scenario within a larger argument.

---

questions.statement: Which sentence best summarizes the main idea of the text?

options.text: Artificial Intelligence is a danger to the employment of many people.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text focuses on bias and objectivity, not job loss.

options.text: Algorithmic objectivity is a myth because machines reflect the flaws of their training data.
options.feedback: Correct. This captures the contrast between the belief in math and the reality of biased data.

options.text: Hiring processes should be completely automated to avoid human sexism.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text argues that automation can replicate sexism.

options.text: Diversifying tech companies is only a political goal and has no technical value.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text suggests diversity has practical value in identifying pitfalls.

questions.explanation:
Main Idea Identification. Selecting the most comprehensive and accurate summary of the passage's central argument.

---

questions.statement: The phrase "identifying a statistical correlation" implies that the computer:

options.text: Understands the sociological reasons for past hiring patterns.
options.feedback: Incorrect. A computer only sees numbers/patterns, not "reasons" in a human sense.

options.text: Finds a mathematical link between variables without understanding the underlying cause.
options.feedback: Correct. "Statistical correlation" refers to the link, not the underlying morality or reason.

options.text: Is actively trying to be unfair to a specific group of people.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says it's not "sexist" in the human sense of intent.

options.text: Has been programmed by someone who hates female candidates.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The bias comes from the data, not necessarily the intent.

questions.explanation:
Technical Inference. Distinguishing between mathematical operation and human-like understanding in AI.

---

questions.statement: Based on the text, what would be the most effective way to "identify potential pitfalls" in a new AI system?

options.text: Running the algorithm faster to see if it makes mistakes.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Speed doesn't reveal bias; quality of output does.

options.text: Hiring only the most expensive mathematicians to write the code.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text emphasizes diversity, not just cost.

options.text: Having people from different backgrounds test the system for unfair outcomes.
options.feedback: Correct. This aligns with the "diverse group of developers" mentioned in the text.

options.text: Asking the computer itself if it thinks it is being biased.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is logically impossible as the computer doesn't have moral self-awareness.

questions.explanation:
Applying Textual Evidence. Extending the author's logic to a practical scenario of system testing.

---

questions.statement: As robotics ____ more sophisticated, the boundary between human and machine labor is blurring.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Robotics" is treated as a singular field/subject, requiring "becomes".
Correct. Present simple for a general trend with a singular subject.
Incorrect. Would require a plural subject.
Incorrect. "Robotics" is a singular noun in this context.

questions.explanation:
Subject-Verb Agreement. Recognizing that fields ending in "-ics" are usually singular.

---

questions.statement: Some economists predict that by 2040, nearly 40% of current jobs ____ by automated systems.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The "jobs" are not doing the replacing; they are being replaced (passive voice needed).
Correct. Future perfect passive used to describe an action that will be completed by a specific time in the future.
Incorrect. "Predict that" usually leads to a "will" structure.
Incorrect. Doesn't match the future time marker "by 2040".

questions.explanation:
Future Perfect Passive. Describing a completed state in the future where the subject is the recipient.

---

questions.statement: While this may increase productivity, it also ____ questions about how society will support those whose skills are no longer in demand.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Rise" is intransitive; you don't "rise questions".
Correct. "Raise" is transitive and is the standard verb used with "questions" or "issues".
Incorrect. "Arise" is intransitive and usually used for situations starting to exist.
Incorrect. This means to wake someone up or provoke strong action.

questions.explanation:
Confusing Verbs (Rise/Raise). Selecting the correct transitive verb for the idiomatic expression "to raise questions."

---

questions.statement: ____ universal basic income is a solution remains a subject of intense debate.

options.feedback: Incorrect. While common in informal speech, "Whether" is preferred in formal contexts for a subject clause.

La respuesta correcta es C porque "sick" funciona como adjetivo que modifica implícitamente "people" (personas enfermas). Los distractores muestran diferentes usos del adjetivo "sick" y la comprensión de cómo funciona gramaticalmente sin un sustantivo explícito.

---
questions.icfes_type: Interpretación de vocabulario en contexto académico

questions.statement: A student from the coast describes the weather: "In Cartagena, it is usually hot and humid. The temperature __________ around 30 degrees Celsius." Which option correctly fills the blank?
questions.context: Descripción del clima en diferentes regiones de Colombia

options.feedback: incomplete, "is" alone doesn't convey the idea of approximation
correct verb for describing weather conditions
incorrect, "temperature" is singular, requires "is"
incorrect tense, present simple is appropriate for general truths

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es B porque cuando se describe el clima de manera general, se usa presente simple. Los distractores reflejan errores de concordancia de número y confusión de tiempos verbales.

---
questions.icfes_type: Aplicación de vocabulario en descripciones de clima

questions.statement: Gabriel is talking about his hobbies: "I enjoy __________ time with my family on weekends." Which option correctly completes the sentence?
questions.context: Descripción de actividades en tiempo libre

options.feedback: would be correct with different structure
incorrect, "to" followed by gerund is not standard
correct, "enjoy" is followed by gerund
incorrect, "enjoy" requires gerund, not base form

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es C porque el verbo "enjoy" siempre va seguido de un gerundio (-ing). Los distractores muestran errores comunes con verbos que requieren gerundio versus infinitivo, y errores de formación con "to + gerund".

---

questions.statement: The student council is organizing a cultural event. The president says: "We need to decide __________ to have the party." Which option correctly fills the blank?
questions.context: Planificación de eventos escolares en Colombia

options.feedback: incorrect, "when the" doesn't create proper sentence structure
correct, "when" introduces the noun clause
correct, "decide when" is a common pattern meaning choose the time
incorrect, "what" would require different sentence structure

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es C porque "decide when" es una estructura común que significa "decidir cuándo". Los distractores muestran errores en la formación de cláusulas nominales y la selección de palabras interrogativas apropiadas.

---
questions.icfes_type: Uso de vocabulario en contexto de planificación

questions.statement: Two students are talking about a friend who moved to another city. One says: "I miss her. She was my __________ friend in the whole school." Which option correctly fills the blank?
questions.context: Conversación sobre relaciones interpersonales en el entorno escolar

options.feedback: incorrect, "well" is an adverb, needs adjective here
incorrect, "better" implies comparison of two, not superlative
correct superlative form, "the best" indicates highest degree
incorrect, "good" is positive degree, not superlative

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es C porque "best" es la forma superlativa de "good", necesaria cuando se indica el grado más alto entre tres o más opciones. Los distractores muestran errores comunes con grados comparativos y superlativos.

---
questions.icfes_type: Análisis de vocabulario en contexto social

questions.statement: A student is describing a problem and its solution: "There was a noise in the classroom, so we __________ the window to see what was happening outside." Which option correctly completes the sentence?
questions.context: Discusión sobre problemas cotidianos y soluciones en la escuela

options.feedback: incorrect, "open" is present tense, needs past for narrative
correct past simple, matches narrative structure
incorrect, present perfect doesn't fit past narrative context
incorrect, past continuous doesn't match the sequence of events

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es B porque la narración de eventos pasados en secuencia requiere past simple. Los distractores muestran confusión entre diferentes tiempos verbales y su uso en narrativas.

---
questions.icfes_type: Uso de vocabulario en contexto de resolución de problemas

questions.statement: During a debate about technology in education, a student says: "In my opinion, students __________ use tablets in class because it helps them learn in a more interactive way." Which option correctly completes the sentence?
questions.context: Debate académico sobre tecnología en educación colombiana

options.feedback: incorrect, redundant "to" after modal
correct use of modal followed by base verb
correct, "can" is the appropriate modal for expressing ability/permission
incorrect, "caned" is not a word

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es C porque los verbos modales siempre van seguidos de la forma base del verbo sin "to". Los distractores muestran errores comunes con la estructura de los verbos modales.

---
questions.icfes_type: Evaluación de vocabulario en contexto de expresión de opiniones

questions.statement: A student describes her experience visiting the Eje Cafetero: "The coffee region was beautiful. The landscapes were amazing. I __________ have visited the Coffee Park." Which option correctly completes the sentence?
questions.context: Descripción de experiencias de viajes por Colombia

options.feedback: incorrect use, "must have" would express speculation about past
incomplete, modal "can" doesn't work with perfect infinitive
correct, "should have" expresses recommendation about unfulfilled past action
incorrect, "might to" is not valid structure

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta es C porque "should have + past participle" expresa un arrepentimiento o recomendación sobre algo que no se hizo en el pasado. Los distractores muestran errores con estructuras de infinitivos perfectos y formas modales incorrectas.

---
questions.icfes_type: Análisis de vocabulario y expresiones idiomáticas

questions.statement: A student is writing in their English journal about a difficult situation. They write: "When I didn't understand the assignment, I felt frustrated, but my teacher explained it again and I finally __________ it." Which option correctly fills the blank?
questions.context: Escritura de diario sobre experiencias de vida en Colombia

options.feedback: incorrect, "understanded" is not standard past tense
incorrect, present tense doesn't fit past narrative
correct past tense of "understand", irregular verb
incorrect, gerund doesn't fit the sentence structure

questions.explanation: La respuesta correcta es C porque "understood" es el past tense irregular correcto del verbo "understand". Los distractores muestran errores comunes con la formación del past tense de verbos irregulares y la confusión entre formas verbales.
questions.icfes_type: Producción de vocabulario en contexto de narrativa personal

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "I usually wake up at 6:00 __________ in the morning."
questions.context: Situaciones diarias de estudiantes colombianos

options.feedback: "in the morning" is the correct collocation with the specific time of 6:00 AM
Incorrect preposition; we say "in the morning," not "at the morning"

questions.explanation:
The correct collocation is "in the morning." In English, we use "in" with parts of the day (in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening) but "at" with specific times (at 6:00). Common error: Colombian students often confuse prepositions with time expressions.
